verdict: CSX hauled 5% more freight and turned a 12% jump in revenue into a 44% rise in operating income, because total costs were flat even though fuel got much pricier and last year's $164M goodwill charge did not repeat.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +12% YoY — a quarterly record for CSX

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: +54% YoY vs $0.37; vs $0.44 a year ago after removing that quarter's goodwill charge

kpis.label: Operating income
kpis.note: Operating margin 39.1%, up from 30.3% a year ago

kpis.label: Total volume
kpis.note: +5% YoY — intermodal volume rose 7% to 820,000 units

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.note: Chemicals and related products hauled by rail — the single biggest market. Volume rose 7% on more petcoke, waste, plastics and crude oil shipments.

segments.name: Agricultural and food products
segments.note: Grains, feed and other farm and food shipments. Volume rose 4% on domestic and export grain, partly offset by less ethanol.

segments.name: Minerals
segments.note: Limestone, construction materials and other minerals. Revenue rose on pricing even though volume slipped 1%.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Finished vehicles and parts. Volume fell 2% because of a temporary outage at a customer plant that was re-tooling.

segments.name: Metals and equipment
segments.note: Steel, aluminum and machinery. Volume rose 12% — the fastest merchandise growth in the quarter.

segments.name: Forest products
segments.note: Lumber, building products, pulp and paper. Lumber and building products rose, helped by a tighter trucking market.

segments.name: Fertilizers
segments.note: Fertilizer shipments — the only merchandise line that shrank, as higher input costs cut demand. Volume fell 13%.

segments.name: Intermodal
segments.note: Shipping containers that move by rail and truck. Volume rose 7% on domestic customer wins and new services.

segments.name: Coal
segments.note: Coal for export and for US power plants and steelmakers. Export coal rose; domestic coal for utilities fell.

segments.name: Trucking
segments.note: The Quality Carriers trucking business — liquid bulk chemicals hauled by road. Growth was mainly higher fuel surcharges.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Everything else, mainly fees for intermodal storage and equipment use.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Wear and tear on locomotives, track and equipment, spread over their working lives. It fell slightly after an equipment depreciation study, even though the asset base grew.

otherDetail: Other expense was $186M, net: $207M of interest expense on the railroad's debt, partly offset by $21M of other income (mainly pension-related credits and investment income).

takeaways.title: Record revenue, on more freight and higher prices
takeaways.text: Revenue hit a record $4.02B, up 12%. Total volume rose 5% to 1.69M units, and pricing and fuel surcharges — extra charges that rise with diesel prices — added the rest. Intermodal revenue jumped 20% and merchandise revenue 11%.

takeaways.title: Costs stayed flat, so the margin leapt
takeaways.text: Total operating costs were $2.45B, down 2%, even though fuel costs jumped $170M as locomotive diesel prices rose 67%. Purchased services fell $73M on efficiency savings, and last year's $164M goodwill impairment (a write-down of an earlier acquisition) did not repeat. Operating margin widened from 30.3% to 39.1%.

takeaways.title: Profit rose by half
takeaways.text: Net earnings were $1.05B, up 52% from $694M a year ago, and EPS rose 54% to $0.57. Against last year's adjusted figures (which strip out the goodwill charge), operating income still rose 25% and EPS 30%.

footerNote: Railroads do not report gross profit; cost of revenue here = direct train-running costs.
follow100Note: Cost of revenue breaks down as labor and fringe $834M, fuel $451M, purchased services and other $657M, and equipment and other rents $92M. Depreciation is the only remaining operating-expense line, so every expense line sits in exactly one bucket and revenue less total operating expenses equals the reported $1,570M operating income.
